paper_sections.title: Binge Eating (BE) and Obesity: Brain Activity and Psychological Measures before and after Roux-En-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB)
3.4.3. Change in Activation from Baseline to 4 Months Post (T1 > T2)

description.value: The study examined brain responses to food and non-food visual cues, binge-eating status, psychological measures, and changes before and four months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass compared with a non-treatment control group.

design.value: A prospective longitudinal fMRI study compared 15 women with obesity who underwent RYGB with 13 BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment. Participants were assessed approximately one month before and four months after surgery, or at matched time intervals for the non-treatment group. Participants were also classified as binge eating or non-binge eating.

name.value: Questionnaire of Eating and Weight Patterns Revised (QEWP-R)

description.value: Used to assess binge-eating status at baseline and four months.
Used at baseline as part of the assessment of binge-eating status.
Used at four months to reassess binge-eating status; it includes modified questions pertaining to bariatric surgery in place of the EDE-Q.
Participants were assessed according to DSM-5 criteria and classified as BE or NB.

The EMAQ assesses emotional eating in response to both positive and negative emotions and situations. It contains 22 questions, with mean scores calculated for positive emotions and situations and negative emotions and situations.

The PFS assesses the impact of current food-abundant environments, including appetite-related thoughts, feelings, and motivations, at three levels of food proximity: food available, food present, and food tasted.
Body weight was measured at baseline and four months post-surgery.

task_name.value: visual food and non-food cue fMRI paradigm

task_description.value: Participants viewed high energy-density food, low energy-density food, and non-food stimuli in the scanner in six runs. Each run consisted of 10 stimuli of the same type, repeated twice with different stimuli, with stimulus types presented in a pseudorandom order and nonconsecutive runs of each type.

stimuli.value: HEF stimuli included cakes, ice cream, and fast foods. LEF stimuli consisted of fruits and vegetables. NF stimuli consisted of basic office supplies, such as tape, staplers, and rubber bands. All HEF stimuli had an energy density of at least 3.5 kcal/g, and all LEF stimuli had an energy density less than 1 kcal/g.

acquisition_duration_seconds.value: 132 seconds (two minutes and 12 s per run)

instrument.value: 1.5 GE Tesla twin-speed scanner with supine quadrature RF head coil

description.value: Functional T2*-weighted images were obtained with a gradient echo pulse sequence. Scans were collected in six runs. Each run contained 36 whole-brain scans, each consisting of 25 contiguous slices parallel to the AC/PC line. The first three scans of each run were discarded to attain magnetic equilibration.

Prior to statistical analyses, the realigned T2*-weighted volumes were slice-time corrected, spatially transformed to a standardized brain (Montreal Neurologic Institute), and smoothed with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: At baseline, the effect of binge eating status on two emotional eating measures and three PFS measures was tested with baseline BMI as a covariate.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), 21st and 22nd Editions

model_settings.value: Four-month outcome psychological measures were analyzed with the baseline score entered as a covariate. Treatment and binge eating status were entered as fixed factors. F tests and post hoc t tests examined the effect of RYGB versus NT in BE and NB groups.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), 21st and 22nd Editions

model_settings.value: The first-level regressors were created by convolving the onset of each condition with the canonical HRF with duration of 40 s. Contrasts were created for Food > Non-Food (NF) and High Energy Density Food (HEF) > Low Energy Density Food (LEF) at baseline (T1), four months post (T2), and T1 > T2.

model_type.value: group random effects (2nd-level) multiple regression analyses

model_settings.value: Contrasts of parameter estimates from the first-level within-subject models were passed to second-level multiple regression analyses. Predictor variables were experimental group (BE vs. NB) and intervention group (RYGB vs. NT), with BMI as a nuisance covariate. Main comparisons included overall effects at T1, T2, and T1 > T2, and two-way interactions between experimental and intervention groups.

estimator.value: nonparametric bootstrapping; one thousand bootstrap samples using a bias corrected and accelerated confidence interval
